newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 14.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Twenty-four prisoners have died since June in the MACA prison in Abidjan, most of them victims of cholera. Officials say the victims had been drinking stagnant water that was never meant to be consumed.

- Some 16,800 tourists arrived in Ivory Coast by charter plane in the first half of 1997 against 16,000 in the whole of 1996. The government has opened up the airways to charter flights since 1993 in an effort to attract 500,000 tourists a year by 2000, against 237,000 in 1996.

- Businessmen and officials at a weekend seminar said Ivory Coast must reduce its reliance on commodities, which still provide 66 percent of export income and account for 33 percent of GDP. A policy of diversification has produced results since the 1994 devaluation, which made industrial products more competitive.

- A tender to build a new market in Treichville, the popular quarter of Abidjan, will be launched next week, but the premises will not be ready until the end of 1999. Some stallholders who worked in the old, sprawling market complain they have not been found replacement sites after a fire earlier this year.

- Liberian refugees in Ivory Coast wanting to vote in their country's July 19 election have had to cross back over the border to register, creating big population shifts in the southeast of Ivory Coast. But many people are still too frightened of fresh upheaval to return for good.

- The Ivory Coast soccer team could only draw 0-0 with Benin at the weekend, and must get at least one point from the game against Mali in a fortnight's time to win a place in next year's finals of the Africa Nations cup in Burkina Faso.
